messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 tail latency spike detected in us-east-1 (router path). p95=210ms -> 420ms, p99=640ms -> 1800ms, streaming stalls up 12%. Auto-paging SREs.
Alex G: on it, joining bridge. seeing a clear bump starting ~10:12 UTC.
Tim S (oncall): I'm oncall. paging SREs and eng-runtime. Any customer-facing errors?
CS - Priya: getting reports from 3 enterprise customers about slow streaming responses and reconnects. CS is collecting session IDs.
Rachael L: logs show increased retransmits on router LB and >40% of traffic routed to a small set of backends (hot spill).
Alex G: suspect routing policy bug + hot partition. can someone dump routing decisions for a sample trace?
eng-runtime: running quick query: `SELECT count(*) FROM requests WHERE route = 'model-serve' AND region='us-east-1' AND ts > now() - 10m GROUP BY backend` - result shows 78% to backend-3a.
SRE Jonas: that backend is on a single rack that has been healthy. but routing table weights indicate unexpected bias.
Maria P: I pushed a change to preferLocal last week; might be interacting with hotkey mapping. rolling back small change?
Tim S (oncall): don't rollback yet. we need safe mitigation first: enable router fallback policy to spread requests across cluster and disable streaming-prefetch for affected model.
Alex G: agreed. applying fallback now.
Alex G: `curl -X POST https://router-admin/api/v1/fallback -d '{"policy":"spread","region":"us-east-1","ttl":600}'`
incident-bot: ACTION: fallback policy applied (id=fallback-6222) by Alex G.
Rachael L: telemetry after fallback: p95 -> 280ms, p99 -> 720ms. improvement but still high.
Maria P: rolling out temporary LB weight correction to remove backend-3a from hotset.
eng-runtime: `PATCH /lb/api/weights {"backend-3a":0.05, "rebalance":true}` -> applying
SRE Jonas: after weight adjust p95 170ms, p99 430ms, streaming stalls down to +3% vs baseline.
CS - Priya: confirmed partial mitigation — customers still seeing occasional stalls but many sessions resumed. I told them we're mitigating now.
Tim S (oncall): good. root cause hypothesis: policy conflict between preferLocal rollout + new shard hashing that created a hot spill to backend-3a in us-east-1. need full triage.
Alex G: capturing traces for impacted requests and will look for KV cache eviction patterns. can someone pull router decision logs for backend-3a for last 20m?
eng-runtime: attached snippet: ```
# router-decision excerpt
ts: 2026-03-15T10:12:31Z route=model-serve shard=hotspan key=abc123 backend=3a weight=0.9
ts: 2026-03-15T10:12:31Z route=model-serve shard=hotspan key=def456 backend=3a weight=0.9
ts: 2026-03-15T10:12:32Z route=model-serve shard=hotspan key=ghi789 backend=3a weight=0.92
```
Rachael L: looks like the weight calc is drifting upward for that shard. there's also a fallback loop hitting the same backend repeatedly.
Maria P: I think `preferLocal` + new `stickyShard` heuristic got mis-scored; it amplified a hot key cluster. I'm preparing a revert for that heuristic.
Tim S (oncall): prepare rollback but hold execution until after we stabilize. document mitigation steps.
Alex G: creating a short-lived routing rule to rate-limit requests to the hot shard to prevent head-of-line blocking: `route-rule add limit=200/s shard=hotspan region=us-east-1`
incident-bot: ACTION: route-rule created id=rr-6222 by Alex G.
SRE Jonas: rate-limit looks effective. tail p99 slowly trending down to 360ms.
CS - Priya: pushing customer update: "We've applied mitigations and are monitoring; some customers may still see intermittent stalls, estimated 5% of streaming sessions affected."
Rachael L: collecting additional metrics: KV cache hit-rate on backend-3a dropped 40% during spike. likely cache eviction due to concentration.
eng-runtime: retrieving allocation traces... `alloc_histogram(backend-3a) shows a spike in active tokens at 10:12:25 -> 10:13:10`
Maria P: I'm preparing formal revert PR for the `stickyShard` scoring change. will link in thread.
Alex G: start a canary for the revert in us-east-1a only once PR merged. until then keep fallback+rate-limit.
Tim S (oncall): hooking into live bridge now for coordinated rollback if canary fails.
Rachael L: temporary telemetry note for postmortem: affected region us-east-1, root cause candidate: routing scoring bug + preferLocal interaction -> hot spill -> cache eviction -> streaming stalls and p99 surge.
Alex G: rough customer impact numbers: peak 12k requests/s affected, ~3.2% error/reconnects, 18% increase in median latency for affected tenants.
CS - Priya: adding list of impacted accounts to the incident doc (IDs provided). i'm scheduling customer follow-ups after resolution.
eng-runtime: FYI, we've bumped autoscale floor on model pool in us-east-1 to absorb tail load while we stabilize.
incident-bot: NOTE: mitigation steps executed: fallback policy, lb weight adjust, rate-limit on hot shard, autoscale floor bump.
Tim S (oncall): next steps: (1) merge and canary revert of stickyShard scoring, (2) run long-run simulation to validate no other hot spills, (3) postmortem and SLA assessment. Owners: Maria P (revert), Alex G (mitigations), SRE Jonas (telemetry + postmortem).
Maria P: PR opened: https://git.internal/p/stickyShard-revert/pull/94 — canary target=us-east-1a.
SRE Jonas: collecting long-term telemetry and saving snapshots for postmortem.
Alex G: will update thread when canary completes. good job everyone. :thumbsup:
Tim S (oncall): closing bridge when canary stable. leave channel for follow-ups.
incident-bot: RESOLVED: p99 back near baseline (p99=210ms). incident status -> mitigated; postmortem required.
CS - Priya: customers notified of mitigation and next steps.
Rachael L: saving logs + router trace bundle to incidents bucket: s3://incidents/6222334455/router-traces.zip
Alex G: tagging postmortem assignee and ETA 48hrs.
SRE Jonas: adding action item: add automated detection for sudden backend weight drift to prevent future hot spills.
Maria P: will follow up on a fix for scoring interaction and add extra unit tests.
Alex G: thanks team — closing this thread for now.
